summary: Scope is where in the code a variable can be used. In Python, if blocks and loops do not create a new scope, but functions do.
notes: message is created inside the if and printed after it. This works because the if was True.
bonus exists only inside calculate_bonus(). Using it outside raises NameError.
global total_points lets add_points() change the variable outside the function.
pitfall: Assigning to a global inside a function without global creates a new local variable with the same name, so the global never changes. Using += on it raises UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'total_points'.
